They're really only competing in the sense that investors have a finite amount to put in, so they might split their funds between the two. It uses the same blockchain tech as bitcoin, but has slightly different functionality. Many people early in the bitcoin community understood that BTC is only a prototype, albeit a rather well refined one. Satoshi wanted this tech to go mainstream, and made his software open source so that it could be audited for security, and so that the community could transcend his platform once it became necessary. I don't think he expected the BTC community to manage his invention so well, and from most appearances, BTC is still the most stable/usable of the crypto currencies, despite some vulnerabilities with through 51% and mass transaction attacks.
